pages.title: Blender
pages.summary: The 3D studio at the heart of Animux. Blender 5.2 LTS with Cycles, EEVEE, Grease Pencil and the MPFB character add-on, and how to find your way around it.

pages.title: MakeHuman II and MPFB
pages.summary: Make realistic human characters with sliders, either in the stand-alone MakeHuman II or with the MPFB add-on directly inside Blender.

pages.title: FreeCAD, Wings 3D, MeshLab and OpenSCAD
pages.summary: The other 3D modellers on Animux and when each one is the right tool next to Blender.

pages.title: Renderers
pages.summary: Cycles, EEVEE, POV-Ray, LuxCoreRender, Mitsuba 3, appleseed and pbrt-v4. What each one is good at, how to run its sample scene, and which one to choose.

pages.title: Renderer comparison
pages.summary: The seven renderers in Animux side by side: full name, who makes it, how it calculates light, what it runs on, what it does best and when to use it.

pages.title: Flamenco render farm
pages.summary: Let several computers render one Blender animation together, using Flamenco Manager, Workers and shared storage, and the Animux render farm boot roles.

pages.title: Gaffer
pages.summary: The node-based lighting and look-development tool used by film studios, included with Cortex, OSL, OpenUSD and Alembic, and rendering with Cycles.

pages.title: Pipeline formats and tools
pages.summary: OpenUSD, Alembic, OpenEXR, OpenColorIO, OpenVDB, OSL and MaterialX, what each studio format is for and the tools Animux has for it.

pages.title: Studio formats
pages.summary: OpenUSD, Alembic, OpenEXR, OpenColorIO and OpenVDB, one card each: which studio made it, what problem it solves, and what it looks like in Animux.

pages.title: Synfig Studio
pages.summary: 2D vector animation with automatic in-between frames and bone rigs. Ideal for cut-out characters, motion graphics and explainer films.

pages.title: OpenToonz
pages.summary: The studio 2D animation program: hand-drawn and cut-out animation with the Xsheet, scan cleanup, ink and paint, and node-based effects. New in r16.3.

pages.title: Pencil2D and TupiTube
pages.summary: Hand-drawn, frame-by-frame animation the traditional way, with onion skin, a timeline and export to video or GIF.

pages.title: Krita
pages.summary: Professional digital painting with hundreds of brushes, layers, a drawing-tablet-friendly interface and a full frame-by-frame animation timeline.

pages.title: Stopmotion
pages.summary: Capture stop-motion animation with a webcam or import photos from a camera, check each pose with onion skin, and export a film.

pages.title: GIMP, Inkscape and other image tools
pages.summary: Photo editing with GIMP, vector drawing with Inkscape, sketching with MyPaint, pixel art with GrafX2 and mtPaint, and batch work with ImageMagick.

pages.title: Kdenlive
pages.summary: The recommended video editor on Animux. Put shots and sound on a timeline, add titles and transitions, and export an MP4 for YouTube or a festival.

pages.title: More video tools
pages.summary: OpenShot, Cinelerra-GG and Avidemux for editing, HandBrake and FFmpeg for converting, DJV for reviewing renders, VLC for playing, and screen recording.

pages.title: Sound and music
pages.summary: Record voices with Audacity, mix the soundtrack in Ardour, compose with LMMS, Hydrogen and MuseScore, and understand how audio works on Animux.

pages.title: Upscayl
pages.summary: Enlarge images 2× to 4× and make them sharper with AI models that run on your own computer, offline.

pages.title: AI tools
pages.summary: Speech to text and subtitles (Whisper), background removal (rembg), local chat models (Ollama) and Stable Diffusion (ComfyUI), all running on your own computer.

pages.title: AI agents in Blender, GIMP, Krita and Inkscape (MCP)
pages.summary: Let an AI assistant work in Blender, GIMP, Krita and Inkscape through MCP, offline with a local model or with Claude Code; plus Higgsfield and LTX cloud generation.

pages.title: Storyboards, print and PDF
pages.summary: Plan your film with storyboards in Krita, Blender or Scribus, make an animatic, and lay out posters, scripts and portfolios as PDF.

pages.title: System tools
pages.summary: Backups with Timeshift, disks with Disks and GParted, burning with K3b, system monitors, virtual machines, containers and remote access.

pages.title: Your first 3D render
pages.summary: In Blender, replace the default cube with a monkey head, give it shiny red paint, add a floor, light it and render a picture. About 30 minutes, no experience needed.

pages.title: A turntable animation
pages.summary: Make Suzanne spin once around in four seconds with two keyframes, then render the animation straight to an MP4 video. About 20 minutes.

pages.title: A character with MakeHuman
pages.summary: Create a human character with MPFB inside Blender, give it a skeleton, pose it and set a keyframe, or design it in MakeHuman II and bring it over. About 30 minutes.

pages.title: A bouncing ball in Synfig
pages.summary: The classic first animation exercise. Make a ball fall, squash and bounce with waypoints and ease in and out, then export a GIF. About 30 minutes.

pages.title: Hand-drawn animation in Pencil2D
pages.summary: Draw a short flip-book animation frame by frame with onion skin, play it back and export it as GIF or MP4. About 30 minutes, perfect for beginners and children.

pages.title: Paint an animation in Krita
pages.summary: Use Krita's animation workspace to paint a short loop, such as a flickering candle flame, with onion skins, then render it to a video. About 40 minutes.

pages.title: Stop motion with a webcam
pages.summary: Set up a tiny studio, capture a clay or LEGO animation with Stopmotion's onion skin, and turn it into a video with sound.

pages.title: Edit your film in Kdenlive
pages.summary: Put rendered shots, a title and music together on a timeline and export an MP4 ready for YouTube. Uses the turntable video from the earlier tutorial. About 30 minutes.

pages.title: Command-line rendering and batch jobs
pages.summary: Render Blender, Synfig and POV-Ray without opening them, keep renders running after you log out, render overnight, join frames into a video and convert hundreds of images at once.
